title: Per-layer FP8 scaling + canary observability for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2) activation
creator: Ava Kim
description: Enable controlled FP8 activation for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2) with conservative per-layer scaling margins, cross-batch drift detection, and an observability-first canary to reduce regression risk during rollout.
background: Recent validation runs show that naive FP8 activation yields intermittent per-layer outliers and cross-batch activation drift on large decoder models (seq len 2048+, attention-heavy). Existing calibration pipelines produce global scale/amax values but lack per-layer safety margins and short-window drift detection. We need a pragmatic activation path that minimizes production regressions while preserving cost/latency benefits.
proposed_solution:
1) Compute per-layer scale factors and Amax with a conservative margin multiplier (default 1.15) instead of global multipliers.
2) Add per-layer stability score (variance of amax across calibration batches) and mark layers with instability for guarded fallback (use INT8 or FP16 for that layer).
3) Implement a small canary fleet routing (1% traffic) with per-token accuracy probes and hallucination / perplexity heuristics.
4) Surface continuous drift metrics (per-layer amax drift, quant-activation outliers) in the Console with automated alerts and a canary SLO.
5) Provide an automated rolling rollback that flips unstable layers to fallback modes and reduces batch-size for affected shards.
calibration_plan: Extend calibration harness to emit per-layer amax distribution across N=30 micro-batches
Run calibration on representative prompts: tokens {0..1024}, {1024..2048}, and code-gen workloads
Compute stability_score = percentile_range(amax, 90) / median(amax) per layer
Generate candidate profile with margin_multiplier = 1.15 and fallback_layers list
test_plan: Unit: new calibration library tests for stability_score thresholds and margin math
Integration: end-to-end profile apply on staging dedicated pool with synthetic load
A/B: run canary traffic (1%) vs baseline for 48h capturing per-route latency, token-error-rate, and user-visible end-to-end evals
Quality: run our eval set (translation, summarization, code) and assert micro-delta WER/BLEU/EM within allowed thresholds
Stress: long-sequence (4096) runs to exercise KV cache and observe per-layer drift under continuous generation
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal bench runs and calibration artifact approval (eng + applied-ml signoff)
Stage 1: deploy to canary fleet (1% traffic) for 48h with tickers enabled for drift alerts
Stage 2: expand to 10% if no regressions; run overnight 12h observation
Stage 3: progressive ramp to 50% with automated rollback hooks on SLO breach
Stage 4: full rollout with monitored post-release regression evals and 7-day watch
rollback_criteria: canary_token_error_rate increase > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 30m
per_route_quality_delta exceeds allowed threshold for two consecutive windows
unexpected OOM or decoder KV-corruption observed in staging or canary
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline produces per-layer profile and stability report stored in artifacts
Canary run <48h shows no regressions by defined metrics
Console dashboard shows per-layer drift and alerts configured
Automated rollback test passes in staging (simulated SLO breach triggers rollback)
Documentation updated: runbook + run-calibration command + ops playbook
